A_first_token_threat.verdict: STRONG THREAT, not resolved. The exact quantity the proposal reads (first-assistant-token logits) is independently, mechanistically identified across four 2026-era papers as (a) the specific locus of 'shallow safety alignment' that current alignment methods exploit as a shortcut, (b) a weak causal handle even within that shallow regime (the single onset token carries far less causal weight than the first half of the response), (c) unable to distinguish qualitatively different failure trajectories that produce the same final behavioral label, and (d) specifically unreliable for reasoning/CoT models. None of this is fatal to the proposal by itself (a threshold+slope fit to a known-shallow signal can still be informative), but it means a first-token dose-response curve should be validated against, not substituted for, full-generation behavior, and the proposal's own framing ('anchored levels transfer, unanchored don't') does not address this threat at all -- anchoring calibrates the SCALE, not the DEPTH, of the readout.

papers.title: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep
papers.quote: safety alignment can take shortcuts, wherein the alignment adapts a model's generative distribution primarily over only its very first few output tokens. We refer to this issue as shallow safety alignment.

papers.title: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep
papers.quote: we show that deepening the safety alignment beyond just the first few tokens can often meaningfully improve robustness against some common exploits [...] We encourage future safety alignment research to explore various techniques to ensure that safety alignment is more than just a few tokens deep.

papers.title: Breaking Refusal in the First Half: A Mechanistic Study of the Prefill Jailbreak
papers.quote: restoring the harm signal over the first half of the response recovers refusal as much as the whole response, while the second half recovers almost nothing and the onset token alone only 9%.

papers.title: Breaking Refusal in the First Half: A Mechanistic Study of the Prefill Jailbreak
papers.quote: the model builds a full-strength harm representation on the flipped prompts (probe 0.91-0.98, as high as on the ones it refuses) while behavioral refusal drops to chance ... Refusal is therefore a shallow, response-site computation.

papers.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Temporal Logit Observability for LLM Safety Failures
papers.quote: The same ASR-success label can hide three fundamentally different processes: refusal evidence may have appeared briefly and been suppressed; refusal may have emerged but too late to matter; or refusal may never have been triggered at all.

papers.title: First Token Matters: Understanding Safety Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
papers.quote: while the refusal projection strength of LRMs remains aligned with that of IT models during the prompt encoding phase, it drops sharply at the first generated token ... we term Onset Refusal Collapse (ORC).

B_censoring.expected_censoring: Searched directly for any LLM paper that fits a dose-response/Hill/logistic curve to graded harmful prompts and reports the fraction of models/conditions that censor (all-refuse or all-comply, no 50% crossing); found no such report. This appears to be an open gap in the LLM-safety literature specifically -- the censoring problem is well-documented in psychometrics/pharmacology (see below) but nobody has yet quantified it for LLM dose-response safety curves.

min_dose_levels.answer: No single 'minimum' number is agreed; two different, both citable, benchmarks exist and neither maps cleanly onto a 15-forward-pass, 2-anchor design: (1) the classical LOCALLY D-OPTIMAL design for a 2-parameter logistic model concentrates all weight at exactly 2 dose points (at standardized logit +/-1.5434) -- a theoretical minimum, but it is a LOCAL optimum that requires already knowing the true threshold/slope to place the 2 points correctly, so it is fragile precisely when threshold+slope are unknown a priori. (2) Practical/robust dose-response design guidance recommends many more, non-degenerate levels with replication -- one worked design used 8 central dose levels plus 2 boundary levels (28 total observations with duplicates) specifically to be robust to NOT knowing the true parameters in advance.
min_dose_levels.source: PMC13221392 (Kappenberg et al., 'Simple, robust and near optimal designs for the estimation of log-logistic dose response functions') for the practical-design number; theoretical 2-point D-optimal result via Abdelbasit & Plackett-style logistic D-optimality (surveyed at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11147135/ and https://webpages.math.luc.edu/~tobrien/research/modapaper2007.pdf).
min_dose_levels.quote: requiring duplicates would, after rounding, work out to 28 total observations needed, 2 each for the 8 central doses, plus 6 each for the minimum and maximum doses. [...] The resulting design places observations on the two shoulders of the curve, where a small movement in dose changes the response probability, rather than where the curve is flat.

papers.title: The Refusal Residue: When Probes Catch Alignment Faking and When They Don't
papers.quote: Under leakage-free leave-one-query-out probing, detection survives on Llama (AUROC 0.87) but collapses to chance on Qwen (0.43), and cross-model transfer is null.
papers.note: Concrete numbers for a hidden-state safety-relevant probe: 0.87 within-model vs 0.43 (chance) on a different model family; the paper separately reports that cross-model Procrustes alignment 'is null under a random-Procrustes baseline.'

papers.title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures
papers.quote: monitors do not transfer across deployments without recalibration: calibrated on qwen2.5:7b and deployed on llama3.1:8b over a matched task, tool and injector plan, the primary monitor sits at chance (AUROC 0.527, healthy FA 0.75), while the same target recalibrated on itself reaches 0.885.
papers.note: Direct, numeric cross-family calibration-transfer failure for a safety-adjacent monitor: 0.885 same-model vs 0.527 (chance) cross-family with no recalibration -- this is the exact failure mode the proposal's anchored metric claims to avoid, and sets the size of the effect any 'transfers without recalibration' claim must beat.

papers.title: A Negative Result on Cross-Model Activation Transfer in a Pythia Multi-Hop Setting
papers.quote: Replacement-style injection is consistently destructive, and rescaling translated vectors to the receiver hidden-state norm does not rescue performance ... offline representational alignment is not sufficient for useful causal communication inside the receiver.
papers.note: Not a safety-calibration paper per se, but a clean general-purpose negative result: high cross-model representational similarity (normalized cosine ~0.97) does NOT imply the representation is causally usable after transfer -- a structural caution for any 'this axis transfers across families' claim.

D_existing_competitors.verdict: The proposal's EXACT recipe (two fixed benign/harmful anchor sentences -> single first-token logit read -> Hill-curve ED50/slope fit, no parent, no labels, no generations, ~15 forward passes) was not found verbatim anywhere searched. But the surrounding design space is NOT empty: (1) SelfGrader already does 'anchored...logit' safety scoring per query via ICL anchors, just for per-query jailbreak detection rather than a model-level dose axis; (2) ProbGuard already claims and empirically demonstrates architecture-agnostic, cross-family calibrated safety-risk estimation from early output distributions, with large (79.6%/71.9%) reported calibration gains -- a stronger validated cross-family generalization result than the proposal has yet produced; (3) Fast Proxies for LLM Robustness Evaluation already validates a cheap (single-generation) safety proxy's rank correlation with expensive red-teaming ACROSS model families (rs=0.94) with no parent model; (4) escapement is a live, deployed 'cheap-ish safety score for arbitrary open-weight HF checkpoints' product, though it needs a parent/base model and real generations. SAY PLAINLY: nothing found does the proposal's precise anchored-dose-axis-plus-Hill-slope construction, but each of its three central selling points -- (a) anchoring logits against fixed references, (b) cheap/no-generation safety signal, (c) cross-family generalization -- already has a separate, published, numerically-validated existence proof, which raises the bar for what the combination needs to demonstrate over any one of them alone.

design_changes_implied: Add an explicit per-condition censoring detector (all-refuse / all-comply at every rung) and report the censored fraction by family/model rather than force-fitting an ED50 in those cases; use a Turnbull-style interval-censored NPMLE or report a one-sided bound instead of a point ED50 when censored.

Fit the Hill curve with Firth-penalized (bias-reduced) logistic likelihood, or a hierarchical/partially-pooled Bayesian model across families, rather than plain MLE, given the small number of dose rungs (~15 forward passes) and the near-certainty of quasi-separation at some rungs.

Justify the number and spacing of dose levels explicitly: the 2-point locally D-optimal design assumes the threshold/slope are already known (they are not, here), so use a wider, more robust set of rungs (the dose-response literature's practical designs use ~8-10 central levels plus boundary levels) rather than relying on the theoretical 2-point minimum.

Do not treat the first-assistant-token logit as a ground-truth safety readout on its own: validate it against full-generation judged outcomes and, per the prefill-jailbreak mechanistic literature, against a first-half-of-response window (the onset token alone was shown to carry only ~9% of the causal effect that the first half of the response carries) -- report the attenuation explicitly.

Explicitly exclude or separately stress-test reasoning/chain-of-thought models (e.g. Qwen3-style thinking blocks): the first-generated-token refusal signal is independently reported to collapse specifically at the reasoning-onset token for LRMs, which is exactly the token this method reads.

Pre-register a check for the specific failure the field already worries about (self-correction / late refusal / suppressed-then-recovered refusal) so a favorable (ED50, slope) reading is not mistaken for robustness to prefill or adversarial-suffix attacks, which are documented to defeat first-few-token safety signals specifically.

Set the cross-family 'transfers without recalibration' bar against the documented size of calibration-transfer failure elsewhere (AUROC 0.87->0.43 in one probe study, 0.885->0.527 in one monitor study) and report per-family calibration curves, not only a pooled correlation, so a reviewer can see whether anchoring genuinely closes a gap of that size.

Add SelfGrader (anchored-logit query scoring), ProbGuard (architecture-agnostic distributional-logit calibration, cross-family Brier/ECE gains), and Fast Proxies for LLM Robustness Evaluation (cross-family rank-correlated single-generation ASR proxy) to related work and state precisely what differs from each, since each already has a numerically validated claim on one of the proposal's three selling points (anchoring, cheapness, cross-family transfer).
